title: 2 Things You Didn't Know About the Mercedes G63 6x6

scenes.text: A Mercedes G 63 AMG 6x6 weighs about nine thousand pounds, stands on thirty-seven inch tyres, and was priced at three hundred seventy-nine thousand euros when new. Roughly one hundred were built. In this video we explain two things you probably did not know about it: what it really is underneath, and where its hardware went afterwards. Every figure comes from a named source.
scenes.caption: 2 THINGS YOU DIDN'T KNOW ABOUT THE MERCEDES G63 AMG 6x6

scenes.text: We used Wikipedia's pages on the 6x6 and on the G-Class, Gear Patrol, The Drive, Road and Track via Motor Authority, CarAdvice via Driven Car Guide, MercedesBlog and Carscoops. They disagree in places, for example on power, price and dates. We show the disagreements. Our own maths is labelled as ours.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: WIKIPEDIA · GEAR PATROL · THE DRIVE · ROAD & TRACK (VIA MOTOR AUTHORITY) · CARADVICE · MERCEDESBLOG · CARSCOOPS · DISAGREEMENTS ARE SHOWN · OUR ARITHMETIC IS LABELLED

scenes.text: Secret one. The G 63 AMG 6x6 was not designed as a luxury toy. Wikipedia says it is derived from a six-wheel-drive Geländewagen developed for the Australian Army, with development from two thousand seven. Gear Patrol says it is built on the military version of the G 320 CDI, in partnership with Magna Steyr in Austria.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: DERIVED FROM A 6x6 GELÄNDEWAGEN DEVELOPED FOR THE AUSTRALIAN ARMY FROM 2007 · GEAR PATROL: BUILT ON THE MILITARY G 320 CDI, WITH MAGNA STEYR
scenes.chapter: Secret one: it started as an army truck

scenes.text: The sources disagree on the year. Road and Track, quoted by Motor Authority in November twenty twenty, says the army vehicle was developed in twenty eleven and based on the G 320 CDI diesel. Wikipedia says two thousand seven. We cannot settle it from our sources. By our arithmetic, the two dates are four years apart.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: ARMY VEHICLE DEVELOPED FROM 2007 · ROAD & TRACK (VIA MOTOR AUTHORITY, 3 NOV 2020): DEVELOPED IN 2011 · GAP: 4 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC) · NOT RESOLVABLE FROM OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The military version did not end when the civilian one did. CarAdvice, in its report of the thirteenth of April twenty fifteen, says the Australian Army chassis is different from the AMG version and will continue to be produced. So the civilian 6x6 was a spin-off from a working vehicle, not the other way round.
scenes.caption: CARADVICE (13 APR 2015, VIA DRIVEN CAR GUIDE): ARMY SIX-WHEEL G-WAGEN CHASSIS 'IS DIFFERENT TO THE AMG VERSION AND WILL CONTINUE TO BE PRODUCED'

scenes.text: Wikipedia says the 6x6 was introduced for the thirtieth anniversary of G-Wagen production. It adds that at launch it was the company's largest off-road vehicle and its second most expensive street-legal model, after the SLS AMG Electric Drive. So an army-derived truck was priced above nearly everything else Mercedes sold.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: INTRODUCED FOR 30TH ANNIVERSARY OF G-WAGEN PRODUCTION · LARGEST MERCEDES OFF-ROADER · 2ND MOST EXPENSIVE STREET-LEGAL MODEL AFTER SLS AMG ELECTRIC DRIVE

scenes.text: Where was it built? Wikipedia says Magna Steyr in Graz, Austria. Gear Patrol says the work was done in partnership with Magna Steyr. Wikipedia's G-Class page mentions Magna Steyr only as a general assembler of the G-Class. Neither page gives details of how many workers or hours each unit took.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: BUILT BY MAGNA STEYR, GRAZ, AUSTRIA · GEAR PATROL: 'IN PARTNERSHIP WITH MAGNA STEYR' · HOURS / WORKERS PER UNIT: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Start with the drivetrain, from Wikipedia. It has six-wheel drive with portal axles similar to those on Unimog vehicles. The transfer case has a high ratio of zero point eight seven to one and a low ratio of two point one six to one. Power is nominally split thirty, forty and thirty percent between the front, middle and rear axles.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 6x6 PORTAL AXLES SIMILAR TO UNIMOG · TRANSFER CASE 0.87:1 HIGH / 2.16:1 LOW · NOMINAL 30:40:30 SPLIT FRONT:MIDDLE:REAR
scenes.chapter: What the army truck gives the owner

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, a thirty, forty, thirty split of the five hundred sixty-one pound-feet of engine torque would be about one hundred sixty-eight, two hundred twenty-four and one hundred sixty-eight pound-feet at each axle. That ignores gearing and losses, so it only shows the idea of the split. Brabus, on its modified car, also lists a thirty, forty, thirty division.
scenes.caption: 561 LB-FT × 30% = 168 · × 40% = 224 · × 30% = 168 (OUR ARITHMETIC; IGNORES GEARING AND LOSSES) · CARSCOOPS: BRABUS CAR ALSO 30/40/30

scenes.text: Five electronic differential locks can lock all six wheels, Wikipedia says. Gear Patrol puts it as up to one hundred percent lock-up across all six wheels, with low-range gearing. Road and Track repeats five differential locks and one hundred percent lockup on all axles. Three outlets give the same claim, which is consistent, although none measured it.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA · GEAR PATROL · ROAD & TRACK: FIVE DIFFERENTIAL LOCKS, UP TO 100% LOCK-UP ON ALL AXLES · MANUFACTURER CLAIM, NOT INDEPENDENTLY MEASURED

scenes.text: The tyre system is unusual. Wikipedia says an air compressor fills four twenty-litre tanks, allowing the driver to change tyre pressure in under twenty seconds. By our arithmetic, four twenty-litre tanks hold eighty litres in total, about twenty-one US gallons by volume. Road and Track also mentions a central tyre-pressure system.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: COMPRESSOR + 4 × 20 L TANKS · PRESSURE CHANGE IN UNDER 20 S · 4 × 20 = 80 L ≈ 21 US GAL (OUR ARITHMETIC) · ROAD & TRACK: CENTRAL TYRE-PRESSURE SYSTEM

scenes.text: Next, the wheels. Wikipedia lists thirty-seven inch tyres, which is nine hundred forty millimetres, on eighteen inch beadlock wheels. Gear Patrol says thirty-seven inch wheels, which is probably a loose use of the word. We follow Wikipedia and Road and Track, which both say tyres. The Brabus car in Carscoops wore Nitto Ridge Grappler tyres.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 37-IN (940 MM) TYRES ON 18-IN BEADLOCK WHEELS · GEAR PATROL SAYS '37-INCH WHEELS' (LIKELY LOOSE WORDING — OUR READING) · CARSCOOPS (BRABUS CAR): 18-IN HUTCHINSON BEADLOCKS, 37-IN NITTO RIDGE GRAPPLER

scenes.text: Ground clearance is four hundred sixty millimetres, which is eighteen point one inches, according to Wikipedia. Road and Track also says eighteen point one inches. Wading depth is one thousand millimetres, or thirty-nine point four inches. Those are manufacturer-type numbers, and our sources do not describe any independent test of either.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: GROUND CLEARANCE 460 MM (18.1 IN) · WADING 1,000 MM (39.4 IN) · ROAD & TRACK: 18.1 IN · INDEPENDENT TESTS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The size. Wikipedia lists a length of fifty-eight seventy-five millimetres, a width of twenty-one ten, and a height of twenty-two ten. By our arithmetic, that is about nineteen point three feet long, six point nine feet wide, and seven point two feet tall. The wheelbase, front axle to rearmost axle, is forty-one ninety-six millimetres, or about thirteen point eight feet.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 5,875 × 2,110 × 2,210 MM · = 19.3 × 6.9 × 7.3 FT · WHEELBASE 4,196 MM = 13.8 FT (OUR CONVERSIONS)

scenes.text: Weight. Wikipedia lists a kerb weight of forty-eighty-three kilograms, which is nine thousand and one pounds. The Drive, describing a specific car in November twenty twenty, says nine thousand fifty pounds. CarAdvice says about four tonnes. These agree within about one percent, and they are all heavy.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 4,083 KG = 9,001 LB · THE DRIVE: 9,050 LB · CARADVICE: 'ABOUT 4 TONNES' · 9,050 vs 9,001 = 0.5% DIFFERENCE (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Put that against the engine. The 5.5-litre twin-turbo V8 makes five hundred thirty-six horsepower, per Wikipedia. By our arithmetic, that is about seven point six kilograms for every horsepower, or about sixteen point eight pounds. Our sources give no comparison car, so we leave it as a number.
scenes.caption: 4,083 KG ÷ 536 HP = 7.6 KG/HP · 9,001 LB ÷ 536 = 16.8 LB/HP (OUR ARITHMETIC; NO COMPARISON CAR IN OUR SOURCES)

scenes.text: The performance numbers. Wikipedia lists zero to sixty miles per hour in seven point eight seconds, and a top speed limited to one hundred miles per hour, which is one hundred sixty-one kilometres per hour. Its text elsewhere says zero to one hundred kilometres per hour in six seconds, while its table lists seven point nine. The page contradicts itself.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 0–60 MPH 7.8 S · TOP SPEED LIMITED TO 100 MPH (161 KM/H) · TEXT: 0–100 KM/H IN 6 S vs TABLE 7.9 S → INTERNAL CONFLICT

scenes.text: Power figures also vary by outlet. Wikipedia lists five hundred forty-three PS, which is five hundred thirty-six horsepower, and five hundred sixty-one pound-feet. Road and Track says five hundred forty-four horsepower and five hundred sixty. CarAdvice gives four hundred five kilowatts and seven hundred sixty newton-metres. The differences are mostly unit rounding.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA 543 PS / 536 HP / 561 LB-FT · ROAD & TRACK 544 HP / 560 LB-FT · CARADVICE 405 KW / 760 N·M (WIKIPEDIA'S G-CLASS PAGE: 400 KW) · DIFFERENCES ARE MAINLY UNIT ROUNDING

scenes.text: One number looks doubtful. Wikipedia's G-Class page lists fuel consumption of fifteen point six litres per hundred kilometres for the 6x6, but the cell is partly garbled in our copy. By our arithmetic, that is about fifteen miles per gallon. For a nine-thousand-pound truck with thirty-seven-inch tyres, we do not trust it without a better source.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (G-CLASS PAGE): 15.6 L/100 KM, CELL PARTLY GARBLED · = 15.1 MPG US (OUR CONVERSION) · NOT CONFIRMED BY ANOTHER SOURCE · NOT USED AS FACT

scenes.text: How many were built? Wikipedia's 6x6 page says production exceeded one hundred vehicles. Its G-Class page says slightly more than one hundred, with the last customer delivery in May twenty fifteen. CarAdvice says roughly one hundred. The Drive says around one hundred. Road and Track says about one hundred. MercedesBlog calls it a never-known-for-sure number of one hundred.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 'EXCEEDING 100' / 'SLIGHTLY MORE THAN 100' · CARADVICE: ROUGHLY 100 · THE DRIVE: AROUND 100 · R&T: ABOUT 100 · MERCEDESBLOG: 'NEVER-KNOWN-FOR-SURE NUMBER OF 100' · EXACT COUNT: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: When did it sell out? CarAdvice, in April twenty fifteen, says the limited run sold out in about twelve months. Wikipedia says Mercedes declared it sold out in early twenty fifteen, and that it sold more units than originally anticipated. By our arithmetic, a twelve month sell-out from a fall twenty thirteen sales start would be about autumn twenty fourteen.
scenes.caption: CARADVICE (13 APR 2015): SOLD OUT IN 'ABOUT 12 MONTHS' · WIKIPEDIA: SOLD OUT EARLY 2015, MORE THAN ANTICIPATED · GEAR PATROL: SALE PLANNED FALL 2013 → +12 MONTHS ≈ AUTUMN 2014 (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Two customer groups are named by Wikipedia. In Malaysia, fifteen right-hand-drive units were bought by Naza World, priced at three point two million ringgit before tax. In South Africa, a businessman ordered ten units, converted to right-hand drive. The Malaysian price cites an article about a Brabus car, so we treat it with caution.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: MALAYSIA — 15 RHD UNITS, NAZA WORLD, RM3.2 MILLION BEFORE TAX (CITED ARTICLE CONCERNS A BRABUS CAR — CAUTION) · SOUTH AFRICA — 10 UNITS ORDERED BY A BUSINESSMAN, CONVERTED TO RHD

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, fifteen plus ten is twenty-five units, which is roughly a quarter of a production of about one hundred. If the Wikipedia count is correct, then those two orders alone account for a large share of the world's 6x6s. Our sources do not tell us where the rest went, except for single cars in Japan and the United States.
scenes.caption: 15 + 10 = 25 ≈ 25% OF ~100 (OUR ARITHMETIC; WIKIPEDIA CUSTOMER FIGURES) · OTHER MARKETS: ONLY JAPAN AND USA CARS MENTIONED (THE DRIVE, CARSCOOPS)

scenes.text: What did it cost new? Carscoops says a sticker price of three hundred seventy-nine thousand euros, the equivalent of five hundred eleven thousand dollars in two thousand thirteen. CarAdvice also says three hundred seventy-nine thousand euros, and nearly five hundred fifty thousand in dollars. Gear Patrol, in March twenty thirteen, said about five hundred twenty-six thousand dollars.
scenes.caption: €379,000 (CARSCOOPS, CARADVICE) · CARSCOOPS: ≈ $511,000 IN 2013 · CARADVICE: 'NEARLY $550,000' · GEAR PATROL (1 MAR 2013): ~$526,000 · EXCHANGE RATES VARY BY OUTLET

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the three dollar figures imply euro to dollar rates of about one point three five, one point four five and one point three nine. They differ because the outlets converted at different dates and rates, and CarAdvice's currency is not stated on the page. The only price we can state firmly is the euro one, repeated by two sources.
scenes.caption: $511,000 ÷ €379,000 = 1.35 · $550,000 ÷ €379,000 = 1.45 · $526,000 ÷ €379,000 = 1.39 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · THE EURO PRICE IS REPEATED BY TWO SOURCES

scenes.text: Used prices climbed. The Drive reports a twenty fourteen car sold for nine hundred one thousand, three hundred thirty-seven dollars on Bring a Trailer in November twenty twenty, close to twice the new price, it says. Motor Authority, a week earlier, reported a bid of five hundred sixty-seven thousand, and said secondhand listings ranged from nine hundred seventy-five thousand to one point six million.
scenes.caption: THE DRIVE (10 NOV 2020): 2014 CAR SOLD $901,337 ON BRING A TRAILER, 'NEAR TWICE' NEW PRICE · MOTOR AUTHORITY (3 NOV 2020): BID $567,000 AT PUBLICATION · LISTINGS $975,000–$1.6 MILLION

scenes.text: A Brabus-tuned example shows the market moving. Carscoops, in December twenty twenty-one, said a Brabus car with eight thousand miles was set to sell for at least one point one million dollars. MercedesBlog, in May twenty twenty-two, said it sold for one million, one hundred seventy thousand, which was one hundred eighty thousand less than its previous price of one million, three hundred fifty thousand.
scenes.caption: CARSCOOPS (21 DEC 2021): BRABUS B63S-700 6x6, 8,000 MI, 'AT LEAST $1.1 MILLION' · MERCEDESBLOG (18 MAY 2022): SOLD $1,170,000 vs PREVIOUS $1,350,000 → −$180,000 · 700 HP / 708 LB-FT

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the drop from one million, three hundred fifty to one million, one hundred seventy is thirteen point three percent. And one point one seven million is about two point three times the five hundred eleven thousand dollar figure. This is one car, resold twice, which is not a market index.
scenes.caption: $180,000 ÷ $1,350,000 = 13.3% DROP · $1,170,000 ÷ $511,000 = 2.29× (OUR ARITHMETIC; ONE CAR, TWO SALES; BRABUS MODIFIED)

scenes.text: Inside, Gear Patrol says the 6x6 seats four, with diamond-quilted leather seats and carbon fibre trim, and bench seats in the pickup bed. The Drive describes a specific car with Designo black leather, red contrast stitching, porcelain accents and an Alcantara headliner. So the army truck's cabin is a luxury one.
scenes.caption: GEAR PATROL: SEATS FOUR · DIAMOND-QUILTED LEATHER · CARBON FIBRE TRIM · BENCH SEATS IN THE BED · THE DRIVE (ONE CAR): DESIGNO BLACK LEATHER, RED STITCHING, PORCELAIN ACCENTS, ALCANTARA HEADLINER

scenes.text: Gear Patrol is blunt about the idea, writing that the 6x6 is clearly the biggest kind of compensation for shortcomings. That is a joke from a magazine, not a fact, and we mark it as opinion. The same piece says it has enough torque to warp the earth's crust, which is also a joke. The measured torque is five hundred sixty-one pound-feet.
scenes.caption: GEAR PATROL (2013): JOKES ABOUT COMPENSATION AND TORQUE — OPINION, NOT FACT · MEASURED / CLAIMED TORQUE: 561 LB-FT (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Brabus took the same truck further. Carscoops describes a B63S-700 package with larger turbocharger compressor wheels, larger exhaust manifolds and an extra water-cooled intercooler, giving seven hundred horsepower and seven hundred eight pound-feet. By our arithmetic, that is thirty point six percent more power and twenty-six percent more torque than the five hundred thirty-six and five hundred sixty-one of the standard truck.
scenes.caption: CARSCOOPS: BRABUS B63S-700 — 700 HP / 708 LB-FT · +164 HP = +30.6% · +147 LB-FT = +26.2% vs 536 HP / 561 LB-FT (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Carscoops also lists Brembo brakes at all six wheels, Ohlins gas bypass shocks, stiffer springs and heavy-duty bump stops on that car. Our sources do not say what the Brabus package cost, how many cars were converted, or how its zero to sixty time compares. The only figure for it is the sale price we mentioned.
scenes.caption: CARSCOOPS: BREMBO BRAKES AT ALL SIX WHEELS · OHLINS GAS BYPASS SHOCKS · STIFFER SPRINGS · HEAVY-DUTY BUMP STOPS · BRABUS PACKAGE PRICE / COUNT / 0–60: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: A note on the gearbox. Wikipedia lists a seven-speed 7G-tronic automatic, and Gear Patrol mentions a low-range transfer case. By our arithmetic, a low range of two point one six against a high range of zero point eight seven multiplies the gearing by about two point five. That is how a road engine crawls over rocks, though Mercedes has not published a crawl speed in our sources.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 7G-TRONIC 7-SPEED · TRANSFER CASE 0.87:1 HIGH, 2.16:1 LOW · 2.16 ÷ 0.87 = 2.48× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · CRAWL SPEED: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Let us check the claim that used 6x6s sold for close to twice the new price. The Drive's sale was nine hundred one thousand, three hundred thirty-seven dollars. Against the five hundred eleven thousand dollar equivalent, by our arithmetic, that is one point seven six times. Against Gear Patrol's five hundred twenty-six thousand it is one point seven one. So nearly twice is generous.
scenes.caption: $901,337 ÷ $511,000 = 1.76× · ÷ $526,000 = 1.71× · ÷ $550,000 = 1.64× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · THE DRIVE: 'NEAR TWICE' — A LOOSE DESCRIPTION

scenes.text: Motor Authority's bid of five hundred sixty-seven thousand dollars was, by our arithmetic, eleven percent above the five hundred eleven thousand dollar figure. Its listings range, from nine hundred seventy-five thousand to one point six million, is one point nine to three point one times that same number. Asking prices and sale prices are different things, and these were asking prices.
scenes.caption: $567,000 ÷ $511,000 = +11.0% · $975,000 ÷ $511,000 = 1.91× · $1,600,000 ÷ $511,000 = 3.13× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · LISTINGS = ASKING PRICES, NOT SALES

scenes.text: The Brabus car's mileage is the other signal. MercedesBlog says it covered eight thousand miles in eight years, and that its new owner may drive twenty-five hundred a year. By our arithmetic, eight thousand over eight is a thousand miles a year. That is the opposite of the Japanese car, which The Drive estimates averaged nearly nine thousand, five hundred.
scenes.caption: BRABUS CAR: 8,000 MI ÷ 8 YEARS = 1,000 MI/YEAR (OUR ARITHMETIC; MERCEDESBLOG) · JAPANESE CAR: ~9,500 MI/YEAR (THE DRIVE'S ESTIMATE)

scenes.text: The Drive gives one memorable measure. It says the Japanese car's drive from Soya Bay to Cape Sata, seventeen hundred miles in thirty-nine hours, is a distance it could cover more than five times a year. By our arithmetic, seventeen hundred miles in thirty-nine hours is an average of about forty-four miles per hour. We cannot verify the trip itself.
scenes.caption: THE DRIVE: SOYA BAY → CAPE SATA, 1,700 MI IN 39 HOURS · 1,700 ÷ 39 = 43.6 MPH AVERAGE (OUR ARITHMETIC) · TRIP NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED

scenes.text: One more timing puzzle. Gear Patrol said the sale would start in fall twenty thirteen. CarAdvice says the run sold out in about twelve months. Wikipedia says sold out in early twenty fifteen. By our arithmetic, fall twenty thirteen to early twenty fifteen is about fifteen to eighteen months, not twelve. The sources may be counting from different starts.
scenes.caption: GEAR PATROL: SALE FROM FALL 2013 · CARADVICE: SOLD OUT IN ~12 MONTHS · WIKIPEDIA: SOLD OUT EARLY 2015 → ~15–18 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC) · START DATES MAY DIFFER

scenes.text: Some proportions, from Wikipedia's numbers. Ground clearance of four hundred sixty millimetres against a tyre diameter of nine hundred forty is, by our arithmetic, forty-nine percent. The wading depth of a thousand millimetres is about two point two times the ground clearance. And the truck is taller than it is wide, by about five percent, twenty-two ten against twenty-one ten.
scenes.caption: 460 ÷ 940 = 48.9% · 1,000 ÷ 460 = 2.17× · 2,210 ÷ 2,110 = 1.047 → 4.7% TALLER THAN WIDE (OUR ARITHMETIC; WIKIPEDIA FIGURES)

scenes.text: The production window was short. Gear Patrol wrote about it on the first of March twenty thirteen. The last customer delivery left Graz in May twenty fifteen, according to Wikipedia. By our arithmetic, that is about twenty-six months from the first article to the last delivery, for a vehicle that appeared in two films in that time.
scenes.caption: GEAR PATROL: 1 MAR 2013 · WIKIPEDIA: LAST DELIVERY MAY 2015 → 26 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC) · FILMS: 2014 AND 2015 (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: A simple check on the price ranking. Wikipedia calls the 6x6 the second most expensive street-legal Mercedes at launch, behind the SLS AMG Electric Drive. It does not give that car's price, and our other sources do not either. So the ranking is a claim we repeat, but cannot verify with a number of our own.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 6x6 = 2ND MOST EXPENSIVE STREET-LEGAL MERCEDES AT LAUNCH, AFTER SLS AMG ELECTRIC DRIVE · THE SLS PRICE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES → RANKING NOT VERIFIED

scenes.text: Finally, a point about naming. Wikipedia titles its page Mercedes-AMG G 63 6x6, but its infobox lists Mercedes-Benz as manufacturer. Sources call it G 63 AMG 6x6, G63 AMG 6x6 and 6x6 G-Wagen. We use the first. That is not a trivial point for anyone searching for parts or auction results, since listings use all of these forms.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA TITLE: MERCEDES-AMG G 63 6x6 (INFOBOX: MERCEDES-BENZ) · OTHER OUTLETS: G 63 AMG 6x6 / G63 AMG 6x6 / 6x6 G-WAGEN

scenes.text: Secret two. The hardware was reused. Wikipedia says the Mercedes G 500 4x4 squared used the body of the long-wheelbase five-door wagon on a shortened chassis from the G 63 AMG 6x6. Road and Track says some hardware, including the portal axles, was later used on the G 550 4x4 squared. So the 6x6 acted as a testbed for later cars.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: G 500 4x4² = LONG-WHEELBASE 5-DOOR BODY ON A SHORTENED CHASSIS FROM THE G 63 AMG 6x6 · ROAD & TRACK: PORTAL AXLES LATER USED ON G 550 4x4²
scenes.chapter: Secret two: its parts lived on

scenes.text: The G 500 four by four squared used a four-litre twin-turbo V8 making four hundred sixteen horsepower, according to Wikipedia. Its table lists zero to one hundred kilometres per hour in seven point four seconds. By our arithmetic, that is one hundred twenty horsepower fewer than the 6x6, or twenty-two percent less, in a smaller package.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: G 500 4x4² — 4.0 L BITURBO V8, 416 HP, 0–100 KM/H 7.4 S · 536 − 416 = 120 HP = 22.4% LESS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Mercedes-Maybach G 650 Landaulet took the idea to luxury. Wikipedia says it was shown at Geneva in March twenty seventeen, uses the extended chassis with portal axles and raised suspension from the G 500 4x4 squared, has a V twelve making six hundred twenty-one horsepower, cost seven hundred forty-nine thousand, seven hundred euros, and was limited to ninety-nine units.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: GENEVA, MARCH 2017 · PORTAL AXLES + RAISED SUSPENSION FROM 4x4² · V12 621 HP · €749,700 · LIMITED TO 99

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the Maybach's price is one point nine eight times the 6x6's euro launch price, though they are different cars sold years apart. The pattern is what matters here. Hardware from a military-derived six-wheeler reached a luxury landaulet. Whether that was planned from the start is not in our sources.
scenes.caption: €749,700 ÷ €379,000 = 1.98× (OUR ARITHMETIC; DIFFERENT CARS AND YEARS) · WHETHER REUSE WAS PLANNED: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The shortened chassis also tells us the 6x6's frame was not a one-off. Wikipedia says the G 500 4x4 squared came with raised portal axles and the suspension used for the Maybach. We do not know how many parts are shared in detail, only that Mercedes itself described the link in the way Wikipedia reports it.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: G 500 4x4² HAS RAISED PORTAL AXLES AND SUSPENSION ALSO USED FOR THE MAYBACH · PART-BY-PART SHARING: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The 6x6 became a film star. Wikipedia lists appearances in Beyond the Reach, in twenty fourteen, and Jurassic World, in twenty fifteen. CarAdvice also mentions the thriller Beyond the Reach, starring Michael Douglas. A film appearance is not evidence of sales, and our sources do not claim it drove any.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 'BEYOND THE REACH' (2014), 'JURASSIC WORLD' (2015) · CARADVICE: 'BEYOND THE REACH' STARRING MICHAEL DOUGLAS · SALES EFFECT: NOT CLAIMED
scenes.chapter: The movie and the import loophole

scenes.text: In the United States, the truck was never sold new. The Drive says a car came in from Japan and was made road legal by G and K Automotive Conversion in Santa Ana under the Show or Display rules. Carscoops and MercedesBlog also say Show or Display. Motor Authority says that exemption allows up to twenty-five hundred miles per year.
scenes.caption: THE DRIVE: JAPAN-DELIVERED CAR, MADE ROAD LEGAL BY G&K AUTOMOTIVE CONVERSION (SANTA ANA) UNDER SHOW OR DISPLAY · MOTOR AUTHORITY (R&T): LIMITED ON-ROAD USE, UP TO 2,500 MI/YEAR

scenes.text: MercedesBlog adds that an NHTSA inspection is required until the car is twenty-five years old. By our arithmetic, a twenty fourteen car reaches twenty-five in twenty thirty-nine. At twenty-five hundred miles a year for twenty-five years, that is sixty-two thousand, five hundred miles at most, a ceiling that most owners do not approach.
scenes.caption: MERCEDESBLOG: NHTSA INSPECTION REQUIRED UNTIL CAR IS 25 YEARS OLD · 2014 + 25 = 2039 · 2,500 × 25 = 62,500 MI MAX (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Drive notes that its car had covered about forty-eight thousand, nine hundred ninety miles, only around twenty-five hundred of them in America. The headline says forty-seven thousand, which conflicts with the body text. The Drive estimates the earlier Japanese owner averaged nearly nine thousand, five hundred miles a year. So a 6x6 can be driven a lot, outside the United States.
scenes.caption: THE DRIVE: 48,990 MI IN BODY TEXT (HEADLINE SAYS 47,000 — CONFLICT) · ~2,500 MI IN US · AUTHOR'S ESTIMATE: ~9,500 MI/YEAR UNDER JAPANESE OWNER

scenes.text: What is missing. An exact build count. A reliable fuel figure. A Mercedes statement on why the 6x6 ended. CarAdvice says no reason was given. We have no named customers beyond the two Wikipedia lists, and no maintenance bills. Everything here describes the car as it was reported, and none of it is a test by us.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: EXACT BUILD COUNT · RELIABLE FUEL CONSUMPTION · MERCEDES' REASON FOR ENDING PRODUCTION (CARADVICE: NONE GIVEN) · MAINTENANCE COSTS
scenes.chapter: What our sources do not say

scenes.text: If you have owned or driven one, tell us what we missed in the comments. In the other videos of this series we compare it with the Hennessey VelociRaptor 6x6, ask what a six-wheel truck really costs, and tell the story of how it began. Our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description. Subscribe to Pickup Reality.
